title: Interleaved Span Timeline Workbench — correlated request drilldown
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design a focused workbench for request-level drilldown that surfaces interleaved spans, correlation IDs, and timeline filters within the Redwood Console. The goal is to make it fast for engineers and SREs to diagnose cross-service latency, identify problematic KV-cache or batching behavior, and tie traces to rollout/cost dashboards. This workbench is intended to be an entry point from alerts, pay-per-request cost cards, and rollout failure investigations.
user_stories: As an SRE I want to filter a request timeline by correlation ID and see interleaved spans across services so I can quickly spot tail latency spikes.
As a backend engineer I want to jump from a per-route cost spike into a trace with highlighted expensive spans so I can root-cause tokenization or large-input regressions.
As a PM I want an annotated timeline that shows rollout events and model variant switches so I can correlate regressions with rollouts.
As a developer I want to save a set of filters and a time-window for repeatable postmortems.
As an investigator I want to annotate spans and attach a link to a GitHub PR or runbook directly from the timeline view.
acceptance_criteria: Entry points: trace workbench is reachable from alert detail, route cost card, and rollout incident UI.
Interleaved timeline: render spans from multiple services on a single horizontal timeline with clear service lanes and collapsible groups.
Correlation view: highlight and filter by correlation IDs and allow switching between trace-id and correlation-id groupings.
Span detail pane: selecting a span opens a right-side pane with metadata (service, operation, start/latency, tags like kv-cache-hit, batch-size) and links to related logs/PRs.
Time scrubbing and zoom: supports frame-based zoom with keyboard scrubbing and maintains selected span context while zooming.
Saved filters: users can save a named filter set; saved sets appear in a compact dropdown and can be annotated.
Prototype validated: at least two engineering reviews and one SRE usability session with recorded tasks and success metrics (task completion > 80%).
implementation_notes: Rendering: use consolidated canvas layer for timeline to allow GPU-accelerated pan/zoom; virtualize span rows when >200 services/lanes.
Data model: ingest correlation_id as first-class filter; store per-span meta flags for caching/hotpath indicators for visual badges.
Perf trade-offs: limit real-time live-stream updates to visible time window; show a soft banner when data is truncated.
Accessibility: keyboard focus order for timeline scrubber, spans, and details pane; ensure color contrast for service lanes and badges.
Fallbacks: when KV-cache or batch-size fields are missing, show "unknown" and a link to instrumentation docs.
Integration: wire timeline events to rollout API so rollout markers can be layered and clicked to open rollout diff.
design_decisions: Interleaved vs side-by-side: we chose interleaved single-timeline with service lanes rather than stacked timelines to better surface cross-service concurrency patterns.
Correlation-first filter: correlation_id prioritized over trace_id because our logs/metrics pipelines already annotate correlation_id for multi-request journeys.
Compact lane mode: collapsed lane state persists per-user to reduce noise for customers with 40+ services in a single trace.
Annotations persisted: user annotations are stored as lightweight JSON blobs linked to trace IDs to enable shareable postmortems.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: rendering huge traces (thousands of spans) may freeze the client. Mitigation: progressive summarization + server-side aggregation and client-side virtualization.
Risk: feature creep with rollout integrations. Mitigation: MVP supports read-only rollout markers; edit/annotation of rollout events deferred to next cycle.
Risk: leaking sensitive tags in span detail. Mitigation: redact configured PII tags and show a caution badge linking to data-retention policy.
